name: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd.
business_summary: Maharatna CPSE (71.64% Government of India) that designs, manufactures and overhauls military aircraft, helicopters, aero-engines, avionics and aerostructures for the Indian armed forces. Programmes: Tejas LCA Mk1A (97-aircraft order), Su-30MKI, LCH Prachand, ALH, Dornier, engine MRO. FY26 sales Rs 33,089 cr, OPM 30%, net profit Rs 9,116 cr; other income ~Rs 3,900 cr from large cash. Order book Rs 2,54,538 cr (Mar-2026). Revenue is back-ended (Q4 ~40%).

exposures.mechanism: Order book Rs 2,54,538 cr (Mar-2026) is ~7.7x sales, so +10% domestic orders mainly adds to visibility beyond FY33. Treat +10% orders as +10% of ~Rs 25k cr/yr of new inflows -> +Rs 2,500 cr/yr -> PV-equivalent +3-4% of EV; with a 36x P/E multiple lifting on growth visibility -> ~+5.

evidence.source: https://www.venturasecurities.com / HAL exchange filing AON_ALH 2026-09-08 (via web search)
evidence.note: DAC AoN ~Rs 1.1 lakh cr incl. 138 ALH; ~98% for Indian industry

exposures.mechanism: Defence capital outlay is part of union capex; +10% govt capex growth -> +3% to HAL's inflow trajectory, small valuation effect -> ~+2.5. Overlaps with P_DEFENCE_PROCUREMENT so kept lower.

Exports (Dornier, helicopters, LCA interest, spares) are <5% of revenue today; +1 theme unit = export wins double -> +2% of equity value from option value (India-ASEAN joint production headline 2026-10-16, Equitymaster).

Escalation raises emergency procurement and order timing; defence stocks historically gain on flare-ups (model knowledge, May 2025 episode); effect fades fast, persistence 0.25 on a +12% shock -> ~+3.

Global arms demand and supply-chain tightness for engines; marginal for HAL whose customer is the Indian Ministry of Defence. Pack: Brent beta +1.03 (t=1.7) is a risk-on defence/energy co-movement, not a cost channel.

Imported content (GE F404/F414 engines, Russian kits, avionics) is ~25-30% of material costs; contracts largely escalation-protected or in foreign exchange cost-plus. +3% -> costs +~0.8% of revenue unrecovered ~35% = 0.3% -> EBITDA -1% at 28% OPM; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap ~0.85 -> ~-0.4, rounded -0.6.

GE engine supply (F404 deliveries restarted Aug 2026 with 3 units; 7 received, 10 more expected before Nov 2026 per search summaries) and US-India relations; tariffs/friction risk delaying LCA Mk1A deliveries.
Net cash, huge advances; effect is valuation duration at P/E 36. +25 bp -> ~-1.2%.

+25 bp US 10y -> FPI de-risking and higher EM discount rates; pack shows the opposite sign for Fed funds (+5.68, t=+3.1) but that is a 3-year high-beta co-movement during a rate-cut-to-hold cycle, not a causal channel; disagreement noted, weight kept small and wide.

evidence.note: Fed funds t=+3.1 conflicts in sign

exposures.mechanism: FIIs hold ~9.4% (down from 10.2% in Mar-2026) and DIIs 12.5% rising; PSU defence is a domestic-flow favourite. +$5bn/qtr FPI inflow -> ~+1 via liquidity.

Private/foreign entrants (Tata, L&T, Adani, Bharat Forge consortia) vie for AMCA, MRFA, helicopter and trainer programmes; Citi (2026-09-09) says private-sector concerns may be overdone. +1 unit = loss of one major programme worth ~Rs 40-60k cr of potential inflows (~15% of intrinsic value at risk x 40% prob) -> ~-6.

evidence.note: Citi sees 22% upside, private competition concerns overdone

exposures.mechanism: Titanium/aluminium/steel alloy mainly imported or on escalation clauses; small.
Pack +3.31 per +15% (t=+1.9) is a cyclical high-beta co-movement (beta 1.56) without a fundamental channel; weight shrunk to +0.5.

supply_chain.counterparty: Ministry of Defence / IAF / Army / Navy / Coast Guard

supply_chain.note: 113 F404 engines contracted Nov 2025; deliveries slow, restarted Aug 2026

supply_chain.counterparty: Private aerospace consortia (Tata, L&T, Adani, Bharat Forge)
